text: Six hundred kilometres away, it begins to snow.
Except this snow is grey… and it will never melt.
Volcanic ash isn't soft like smoke. It is shattered rock and glass, sharp enough to sting your eyes and lungs.
And it is heavy. Ten centimetres of wet ash could press up to two hundred kilos onto every square metre of a roof.
Sirens. Roads close. Engines choke as the ash clogs them.
